title: Emphasize a difference / compare two things
subtitle: Rhetorical Synthesis · 43 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **43 of the official questions in Rhetorical Synthesis are this one** — 10 Easy, 24 Medium, 9 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The goal says 'emphasize a difference', 'contrast', or 'compare' two items (types, hypotheses, species, programs).
- Sometimes it is narrowed further, for example 'compare the disadvantages' or 'emphasize the significance of one date relative to another'.
- The notes give parallel facts for each item, often with numbers or opposite traits.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the attribute that the goal restricts you to (disadvantages, size, composition, scope), if it names one.
- 2) Pick the choice that names BOTH items and puts their different values on that same attribute side by side, usually with 'whereas', 'while', or 'but', or with a comparative.
- 3) Reject choices that just list both items or give only one item's value.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Some choices mention both items but never state how they differ ('two types include A and B').
Others give a contrast on the wrong attribute, such as an advantage when the goal asked for disadvantages.
On narrowed goals, the trap is a choice that compares the items on some other feature instead of the one the goal specifies.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Some choices mention both items but never state how they differ ('two types include A and B').
Others give a contrast on the wrong attribute, such as an advantage when the goal asked for disadvantages.
